ROUND ONE BOXING

YOUR
PRIVACY.

Last updated: 4 October 2026

1. About this policy

Round One Boxing provides boxing equipment, private boxing training in Salisbury Heights, South Australia, and online coaching. This policy explains how information is handled when you browse, purchase equipment, submit an enquiry or arrange training.

For privacy questions, access or correction requests, or complaints, use our Contact page and include “Privacy” in the subject. We handle information in accordance with applicable Australian privacy law, including the Privacy Act 1988 and Australian Privacy Principles where they apply.

2. Information we collect

  • Orders: name, email, required phone number, delivery recipient and address, products and selected variants, quantities, amounts, order references, payment method, transaction references and payment status.
  • Enquiries: the details you enter in our contact or training form, including training option, experience, goals, preferred times and message. Contact-form phone details are optional; training enquiries require a phone number.
  • Training: information needed to arrange and deliver coaching. Please avoid placing unnecessary medical or other sensitive information in a general enquiry. If relevant health information is needed, we seek consent to collect and use it for that purpose, unless collection is otherwise permitted by law.
  • Technical information: hosting and payment services may receive your IP address, browser/device information, request details and security logs when you use their services.

We collect details directly from you and receive order and payment confirmations from Stripe or PayPal. The website uses payment-provider checkout; it does not collect or store full card numbers, card security codes or your PayPal password.

3. Why we use information

We use information to fulfil and deliver orders, verify payments, send order notifications, answer enquiries, arrange and provide training, address refunds or complaints, prevent fraud and spam, keep business records and meet legal obligations.

The mandatory checkout phone number is used for order or delivery questions and is included in the paid-order notification. Submitting an enquiry or making a purchase does not, by itself, subscribe you to promotional emails.

You may browse without giving us your name. An order or personalised enquiry needs enough information to process it and respond; without required details we may be unable to provide that service.

4. Service providers and disclosures

Information is shared as needed with providers supporting the service:

  • Netlify: website hosting, server-side order records, form submissions and spam protection. Verified paid orders are submitted to the paid-order form so we can fulfil them.
  • Stripe or PayPal: checkout, payment verification, fraud controls and payment-related disputes.
  • Email services, including Google/Gmail: enquiry and order notifications sent to the business inbox.
  • Delivery providers: recipient, address and contact details needed to deliver equipment.
  • Online coaching providers: the chosen video service receives information needed to connect a session. The platform will be identified before the session.

Relevant information may also be disclosed to professional advisers, authorities where required or authorised by law, or others with your consent. We do not sell customer personal information.

Providers may handle information outside Australia, including in the United States and other countries where they or their service providers operate. Locations vary by provider and service. Contact us for available details. Overseas processing does not remove any obligations we have under applicable Australian law.

Read the provider policies: Netlify, Stripe, PayPal and Google.

5. Browser storage, cookies and fonts

The cart uses your browser’s local storage to remember products and quantities. Checkout uses session storage for the checkout attempt, including the phone number you enter. Clearing browser storage removes locally saved details and may interrupt checkout.

The website loads fonts from Google Fonts, which sends normal connection information to Google when fonts are requested. Payment and hosting providers may use cookies or similar technologies for functionality, security and fraud prevention. Their policies describe their own practices. This website’s current source does not include advertising pixels or analytics scripts.

6. Storage, security and retention

Information is held in the website’s hosting and order services, form records, business email and records used to manage bookings and orders. We take reasonable steps to protect it, including limiting access to people who need it and using the security controls available through our service providers. No internet transmission or storage system can be guaranteed completely secure.

We retain information while needed for the purposes described here, including accounting, disputes and legal obligations. When it is no longer needed and no law requires retention, we take reasonable steps to delete or de-identify it. Copies in provider backups may remain until those backups are replaced under the provider’s retention arrangements.

7. Access, correction and privacy choices

Contact us to request access to your information, correct an error, withdraw consent for an optional use or request deletion. We may need reasonable proof of identity. We will consider the request and explain any legal or practical reason we cannot fulfil it, such as required transaction records. Withdrawing consent does not reverse processing already lawfully completed.

A parent or guardian may contact us about a child’s information, subject to appropriate identity and authority checks. Please discuss under-18 training arrangements before providing a child’s details.

8. Complaints and policy updates

Send privacy complaints through the Contact page, describing the issue and your preferred way to receive a response. We will review the relevant records, seek further details if necessary and respond within a reasonable period, including any action we propose. If more time is needed, we will let you know.

If the matter remains unresolved, you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner for guidance or to complain where it has jurisdiction. This policy does not limit rights provided by law.

We will update this page when our practices change and show the revised date. For a material change, we will also provide an appropriate notice. See the OAIC’s guide to privacy policies for further information.
